purpose: Reference material the investigation assistant works over. Each entry describes a kind of destination money leaves for, and what its presence does or does not imply. Findings that cite a typology cite it by id, so an investigator can read the basis for themselves. A typology describes a category of destination; it never asserts anything about a particular customer.

typologies.label: Virtual asset / cryptocurrency exchange
typologies.description: Cryptocurrency exchanges, digital asset brokers, coin trading platforms, bitcoin ATMs and virtual currency wallets. Money sent to these becomes difficult to trace or recall once converted.
typologies.why_it_matters: Funds converted to virtual assets are effectively unrecoverable, which is why accounts taken over by a third party are frequently drained this way. Equally, a great many people buy cryptocurrency for ordinary reasons.
typologies.investigator_note: Presence alone proves nothing. What matters is whether the customer has done this before, and whether the pace and size fit the rest of their behaviour.

typologies.label: Money remittance and international transfer agent
typologies.description: Remittance agencies, money transfer operators, overseas send services, international wire agents and cross-border payment intermediaries.
typologies.why_it_matters: Cross-border transfers settle quickly and reverse poorly. They are also the ordinary way that millions of people support family abroad.
typologies.investigator_note: Look for whether the corridor and recipient are consistent with the customer's history. A first-ever remittance during a wider change of behaviour reads differently from a monthly one.

typologies.label: Prepaid card, stored value and gift voucher
typologies.description: Prepaid card reloads, stored value top-ups, digital wallet loading, gift card and voucher purchases.
typologies.why_it_matters: Stored value converts account funds into a bearer instrument that leaves no onward trail. It is a common instruction in impersonation and authorised-push-payment scams.
typologies.investigator_note: Repeated voucher or prepaid purchases in short order, especially alongside instructions the customer cannot explain, are worth a direct conversation with them.

typologies.label: Online gambling and betting
typologies.description: Betting platforms, online casinos, sportsbooks, gaming and wagering sites.
typologies.why_it_matters: A sharp rise in gambling spend can indicate financial distress, and gambling accounts are also used to layer funds. Neither inference is safe on its own.
typologies.investigator_note: Consider trajectory rather than presence: a steady modest spend is a habit, a sudden escalation is a change worth understanding.

typologies.label: Peer-to-peer and instant transfer service
typologies.description: Peer-to-peer payment applications, instant transfer services and person-to-person money movement platforms.
typologies.why_it_matters: Instant, irrevocable transfers to individuals are the settlement rail for most social engineering scams, and also how most people split a dinner bill.
typologies.investigator_note: The recipient matters more than the rail. Transfers to a name that has never appeared before, at unusual hours, deserve a closer look than the channel itself does.

typologies.label: Payroll and salary source
typologies.description: Employer payroll deposits, salary credits, wage payments and direct deposits from an employing organisation.
typologies.why_it_matters: A regular credit from a consistent source is the strongest single indicator that an account is being used normally by its owner.
typologies.investigator_note: Interruption of a long-standing salary credit is more informative than its presence. Note it if the pattern stops.

typologies.label: Housing: rent and mortgage
typologies.description: Rent payments to a landlord or property manager, mortgage instalments, housing association and letting agency payments.
typologies.why_it_matters: Housing costs are usually the largest recurring payment an individual makes, and dwarf their median transaction every month without being remarkable.
typologies.investigator_note: Size alone should never flag a housing payment. A change of destination for one is far more interesting than its amount.

typologies.label: Utilities and recurring household bills
typologies.description: Electricity, gas, water, telecommunications, broadband and municipal service payments on a recurring schedule.
typologies.why_it_matters: Stable, modest and predictable. Their continued presence through a period of unusual activity suggests the account is still being used by its owner.
typologies.investigator_note: Useful as a control. If ordinary bills continue uninterrupted alongside suspect activity, an account takeover is a less complete explanation.

typologies.label: Investment and brokerage
typologies.description: Brokerage accounts, investment platforms, securities purchases, bond funds, retirement and wealth management transfers.
typologies.why_it_matters: Investment transfers are routinely large and routinely scheduled. A recurring sweep to the same brokerage is a savings habit, not an anomaly.
typologies.investigator_note: Distinguish a standing arrangement from a first-ever transfer. The former is a plan; the latter, if large and unheralded, may not be the customer's own.

typologies.label: Everyday retail and groceries
typologies.description: Supermarkets, grocery stores, general retailers, pharmacies, fuel stations, coffee shops and restaurants.
typologies.why_it_matters: The texture of ordinary life. These form the bulk of a typical customer's history and define what normal looks like for them.
typologies.investigator_note: Their disappearance from a recent window is as notable as anything new appearing in it.

typologies.label: Subscription and digital services
typologies.description: Streaming services, software subscriptions, cloud services, membership fees and recurring digital billing.
typologies.why_it_matters: Small, fixed and repeating. They anchor the low end of a customer's amount distribution.
typologies.investigator_note: Rarely relevant on their own. Continued subscription billing suggests the account holder's own devices are still in use.

typologies.label: Unclassified destination
typologies.description: A destination that does not resemble any documented category - an unfamiliar company name, an individual, or a counterparty whose nature cannot be determined from the record.
typologies.why_it_matters: An unrecognised destination is not a suspicious one. It is a gap in what the record can tell us, and should be reported as a gap.
typologies.investigator_note: State plainly that the destination could not be characterised, rather than inferring a category from the name.

matching_note: Keywords anchor the offline matching route. The embedding route uses the label and description text instead; both draw on this same document.
